assumptions_i_had_to_make: The legacy is ASP.NET Web API on Framework 4.8 (controller-based) and the .NET 10 target is ASP.NET Core (controller or minimal API) — the request says '.NET 10' without naming ASP.NET Core, which I take as implied.
Data access uses ADO.NET against SQL Server (stored proc), so the modern port uses Microsoft.Data.SqlClient rather than an ORM; I am not introducing EF Core unless the legacy used it.
ANI is a string path segment (caller ID / phone number) bound from the route; 'empty ANI' (W0011) means blank-or-missing after binding, not malformed.
Result codes E0001/W0011 are returned in the response body (a code/status envelope), not as HTTP status codes alone — preserving the body code is the binding requirement.
The channel-gate header name and validation rules already exist in the legacy code and are copied as-is; I am not redesigning auth, only re-hosting it.
balance is a numeric/decimal field and its JSON representation (type, precision) must match legacy output exactly — I will verify rather than assume formatting.

Partner endpoints share the same project/controller but are explicitly excluded; I port only the account path and do not carry partner routes or their dependencies unless shared infrastructure forces a minimal stub.

The generation spec at examples/generation-specs/dotnet-service.md governs the .NET 10 patterns (options validation, health endpoints, Dockerfile, log sanitization) where they apply, but the AccountResponse/result-code contract overrides any spec pattern that would alter the wire shape.

This is a migration-skill job: Phase 1 discovery (find the actual legacy source) precedes Phase 2 generation — I do not yet have the legacy source in this repo, so concrete field types/proc params must be read from it before building.
